'''Alexander A. Voronov''' ({{langx|ru|Александр Александрович Воронов}}) (born November 25, 1962) is a [[Russian-American]] [[mathematician]] specializing in [[mathematical physics]], [[algebraic topology]], and [[algebraic geometry]].  He is a Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Minnesota]] and a Visiting Senior Scientist at the [[Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://db.ipmu.jp/member/personal/670en.html |website=Kavli IPMU |title=Alexander Voronov |department=Our People}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Voronov graduated from [[Moscow State School 57]] in 1980. He received an M.S. in Mathematics in 1985 and a Ph.D. in Mathematics at [[Moscow University|Moscow State University]] in 1988 under [[Yuri Manin|Yuri I. Manin]].<ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=61709&fChrono=1 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref> Alexander Voronov is known for his work on the super Mumford isomorphism (see [[Mumford measure]]), semi-infinite cohomology, operads in quantum field theory (see [[Operad#Swiss-cheese operad|Swiss-cheese operad]]), [[Pierre Deligne#Concepts named after Deligne|Deligne]]'s and [[Maxim Kontsevich|Kontsevich]]'s conjectures on Hochschild cohomology, cohomology of vertex operator algebras, and string topology (see [[String topology#The Batalin–Vilkovisky structure|cactus operad]]). He is a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]{{r|amsf}}, an AMS Centennial Fellow,{{r|amsc}}, a [[Simons Foundation|Simons]] Fellow,{{r|sf}} and a 2010 [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]] (JSPS) Research Fellow.
